## Setting up workspace.  
```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(tidyverse)
library(tinytable)
```
## The first step to obtaining and looking into Upworthy's A/B testing data, which they use to optimize the content on their website, is to read the csv file into R.
```{r}
upworthy <- read_csv("https://osf.io/vy8mj/download")
```
## Now that this data is read in, I can pull out the names. 
```{r}
upworthy |>
  names()
```
## Then, I can pull out the top six results from the data. 
```{r}
upworthy |>
  head()
```
## I am following Alexander in the textbook, but using a different selection criteria ("!" instead of "?") so I am choosing the columns "created_at," "clickability_test_id," "headline," "impressions," and "clicks." The following code chunk makes a new data frame for this restricted data and pulls those columns out and then uses head to show the top six responses to this data. 
```{r}
upworthy_restricted <-
  upworthy |>
  select(
    created_at, clickability_test_id, headline, impressions, clicks
    )

head(upworthy_restricted)
```

## Here is where my code differs from the textbook. Instead of using "asks_questions," I am using "uses_bang." We're looking at the text in headlines, and specifically those headlines that used "!" This chunk is telling R to bring up the data for those headlines that used a "!" and used the same image, in order to remove the effect of the image differences themselves. 
```{r}
upworthy_restricted <-
  upworthy_restricted |>
  mutate(
    uses_bang =
      str_detect(string = headline, pattern = "\\!")
    )

upworthy_restricted |>
  count(uses_bang)
```
## Now, for each text with "!" and each picture, I want to see whether the bang has an effect on the number of clicks. 
```{r}
uses_bang_or_not <-
  upworthy_restricted |>
  summarise(
    ave_clicks = mean(clicks),
    .by = c(clickability_test_id, uses_bang)
  ) 

uses_bang_or_not |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = uses_bang,
              values_from = ave_clicks,
              names_prefix = "ave_clicks_") |>
  drop_na(ave_clicks_FALSE, ave_clicks_TRUE) |>
  mutate(difference_in_clicks = ave_clicks_TRUE - ave_clicks_FALSE) |> 
  summarise(average_differce = mean(difference_in_clicks))
```

## This code will provide a cross tab showing the difference between the average number of click between bang and no bang. 
```{r}
uses_bang_or_not |> 
  summarise(mean = mean(ave_clicks),
            .by = uses_bang) |> 
  tt() |> 
  style_tt(j = 1:2, align = "lr") |> 
  format_tt(digits = 0, num_fmt = "decimal") |> 
  setNames(c("UsesABang!", "MeanClicks"))
```

## This is my histogram. 
```{r}
uses_bang_or_not |>
  ggplot(aes(x = ave_clicks, fill = factor(uses_bang))) +
  geom_histogram(position = "identity", alpha = 0.6, bins = 30) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("deeppink", "mediumspringgreen")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    x = "Average clicks",
    y = "Count",
    fill = "Uses a bang",
    caption = "Data source: Upworthy."
  )
```
